verdicts.decision_note: First concrete failure showing that the required components could not fit within the specified main-board dimensions.
The client permits adjustment of the prototype PCB dimensions to satisfy enclosure fit and connector-access constraints.
Distinct routing failure: the 55×40 mm outline and hole arrangement prevented correct PCB routing, beyond the earlier component-fit failure.
The client establishes a concrete 70×50 mm main-board outline for component rearrangement and routing.
Target-specific implementation claim that all components now fit on the resized board after the earlier fit failure; it does not verify routing.

verdicts.decision_note: The single-board architecture makes the legacy main-board dimensions obsolete; the integrated board is not a valid new scope for this legacy Requirement, and duplicate status attributes are removed.
The client confirms that only one integrated board remains, eliminating the separate legacy main-board fit and routing Requirement.
